venue.name: Seaview Game Farm
venue.description: Seaview Game Farm is a 168 acre working farm on a mile of waterfront at Black Creek, between Courtenay and Campbell River, bought by Paul Pfleger in 1973 and farmed since. Over 200 fallow deer, 25 Scottish Highland cattle, goats and an emu live on the farm alongside hay, crops and greenhouses. There is a small farm store selling farm raised venison, grass fed beef, jams and preserves, open Tuesday to Saturday from 10 to 4, and the farm rents a picnic site with a shelter, a BBQ, a fire pit and beach access for get togethers of up to 100 people. The site publishes no farm tour, no animal feeding and no programme for children.
venue.address: 1392 Seaview Road, Black Creek, BC V9J 1J7

facility_notes.washrooms: The rented site has access to the washrooms. Parties over 50 guests require a minimum of one additional portable toilet due to septic and water limitations. This is not included in the site rental rate and is to be arranged by the customer.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Our Site has picnic tables, shelter, BBQ, fire pit, beach access, parking and access to the washrooms.

restrictions: Parties over 50 guests require a minimum of one additional portable toilet due to septic and water limitations. This is not included in the site rental rate and is to be arranged by the customer.
Pets are welcome and must be kept on a leash and cleaned up after.
venue.hours_notes: The farm store is open for drop ins Tuesday to Saturday from 10 to 4. Appointments can be made to visit the store, or curbside pick up arranged, outside those days and hours by calling the farm. No opening hours are published for the farm itself.
venue.seasonal_notes: The farm is trading. The store hours, the 2026 camping rates and the site rental prices were all live on 2026-09-10. Camping runs all year at three different rates, with a peak season of May 15 to September 20 in 2026. Nothing says whether the picnic site rental is seasonal.
venue.price_year_or_season: The camping rates are labelled 2026. The picnic site rental prices carry no year and no date, so it is worth confirming them when you call.

programs.name: Group picnic site rental
programs.description: The farm rents out a picnic site for get togethers, which it advertises for family reunions, company BBQs and similar. The site has picnic tables, a shelter, a BBQ, a fire pit, beach access, parking and access to the washrooms. For up to 50 guests it is $325 for one to four hours, with $50 for each extra two hours. For 51 to 100 guests it is $400 for one to four hours, with $65 for each extra two hours. The maximum is 100 people, and a party over 50 has to arrange and pay for at least one extra portable toilet because of the septic and water limits. Bookings go through the farm by phone or email. The farm publishes no tour, no animal feeding and nothing about whether visitors can see the deer, cattle, goats or emu.
programs.what_children_do: Eat at the picnic tables under the shelter, and go down to the farm's own stretch of waterfront.
programs.our_note: This is a picnic field for hire rather than a farm visit. Nothing on their site says a group gets anywhere near the animals, which is probably the reason you were looking here, so ask about that before anything else. The fee is for the whole site, not per child, so it only works out if you fill it or share it with another room.
programs.practical_summary: Picnic tables, a shelter, a BBQ, a fire pit, beach access, parking and washrooms come with the site. A party over 50 has to bring in an extra portable toilet at its own cost. Nothing is published about step free access, where a bus would park or what happens in the rain.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $325 is the site rental for one to four hours for a party of up to 50 people, not a per person charge. Each extra two hours is $50. A party of 51 to 100 pays $400 for the first four hours and $65 for each extra two hours, and has to arrange and pay for at least one additional portable toilet.
programs.evidence: The Site can accommodate a maximum of 100 people.

gaps: STILL TRADING, BUT NOT A PETTING FARM ON PAPER. The site was live on 2026-09-10, the store hours and site rental prices were read straight from the live page, and the camping rates are labelled 2026. But the whole of their site describes a meat and vegetable farm with accommodation and a picnic site for hire. It does not publish a farm tour, an animal feeding, a petting area or any children's programme, and it does not say whether a visitor can see the deer, cattle, goats or emu at all. Farm Tours appears only in the invisible keyword list in their page code, and there is no page behind it. Nine likely addresses including farmtours, tours, farm-tours, schools, groups, visit and petting-zoo were all checked in a browser and all returned 404.

THE ANIMALS ARE THE THING TO ASK ABOUT. Their about page says over 200 fallow deer, 25 Scottish Highland cattle, goats and an emu live on the farm. Nothing anywhere says whether a visiting group can look at them, walk near them, feed them or touch them. Until that is answered by phone this is a picnic field with animals somewhere on the property.

PER GROUP, NOT PER CHILD. The $325 is a site rental fee for up to 50 guests for one to four hours. Their page lists it under a guest band rather than saying per group in so many words, so reading it as a whole-site fee is an inference from the way it is laid out, not a quote. If it were per child instead it would be roughly $325 a head, which is plainly not what is meant, but it is worth one sentence on the phone to be sure. The same applies to the $400 band for 51 to 100 guests.
no admission price is published for the farm, because no general admission is offered. The farm store is open to walk into but nothing says the rest of the farm is.

hosts_school_groups and hosts_daycare_groups are unanswered rather than no. The site never mentions schools, daycares or children's groups anywhere. It advertises the site to family reunions, company BBQs and weddings.
youngest age welcomed is not stated.

no lead time, no deposit and no cancellation terms are published for the picnic site rental. Their camping page does give terms, a 25 per cent non-refundable deposit at booking with the balance due 28 days before arrival and no refund inside 28 days, but that is written for camping and has not been applied to the site rental.
months and days for the picnic site rental are unknown, not year round. Nothing says which months or days it can be booked.
the shelter on the picnic site is listed as a facility but nothing says whether it is enclosed or whether a group could get out of the rain under it, so no wet weather answer has been recorded.

step free access, stroller access and bus parking are not addressed anywhere on the site. It says only that the site has parking, and that the farm has two entrances, a North Gate at the end of Seaview Road and a South Gate at the end of Williams Beach Road.
the 2026 off season camping rate is missing from their camping page. The peak and shoulder rates are printed but the off season heading and its dates are followed by no price.
the Show More button at the foot of their gallery page does nothing when clicked, so any further photographs behind it could not be seen.

the images recorded here were opened and looked at in a browser before the hero description was written. The two gallery images keep the site's own alt text, which names the offering rather than describing the picture.
their contact page carries a message form. It was not filled in or submitted.
